items.title: Taking away a mixed number
items.prose: Work without a calculator.
items.question: What is $3\tfrac{1}{3} - 1\tfrac{3}{4}$? Give a fraction.

widget.accept: Any form equal to $\tfrac{19}{12}$, which is $1\tfrac{7}{12}$

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Turn both into improper fractions, then use a common denominator.

byKey.smaller-from-larger: You took $\tfrac{1}{3}$ from $\tfrac{3}{4}$ because it was easier. The sum asks for $\tfrac{1}{3} - \tfrac{3}{4}$, which borrows from the whole 2.

explain.text: As improper fractions, $3\tfrac{1}{3} = \tfrac{10}{3}$ and $1\tfrac{3}{4} = \tfrac{7}{4}$. Over twelfths that is $\tfrac{40}{12} - \tfrac{21}{12} = \tfrac{19}{12}$. That is $1\tfrac{7}{12}$.

items.title: Building 35%
items.prose: Work without a calculator. A desk keeps 35% of a £360 commission.
items.question: What is 35% of £360, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find 10%, then build 30% and 5% from it.

byKey.tenth: You found 3.5%. Moving the point once more gives 35%.
byKey.thirty: You found 30%. Add 5% too, half of the 10%.

explain.text: 10% of £360 is £36, so 30% is £108. Half of 10% is 5%, which is £18. Together that is £126.

items.title: Falling further below zero
items.prose: A desk's P&L is −£3k at noon. By the close it has fallen by another £5k.
items.question: Drag the point to the P&L at the close, in £k.

feedback.correct: Five more to the left of −3.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. A fall moves left. Start at −3 and move 5 to the left.

byKey.rose: You moved 5 to the right, which is a rise. A fall moves left.
byKey.ignored-start: You worked out $3 - 5$. The start is −3, so the fall takes it to −8.
byKey.p: Start at −3 and count 5 steps to the left.

explain.text: A fall of £5k is a move of 5 to the left. From −3 that lands on −8. In symbols, $-3 - 5 = -8$.

items.title: Five prices in order
items.prose: Five fills of a cheap share, in pounds.
items.question: Put the prices in order, smallest first.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare the tenths digit first, then the hundredths.

byKey.d45: You placed 0.45 too early because it has fewer digits. As 0.450 it is the largest.
byKey.d0455: You read 0.0455 as large because of its digits. It has 0 tenths, so it is the smallest.

explain.text: Two prices have 0 tenths, so they are smallest: 0.0455 has 4 hundredths and 0.054 has 5. Among the rest, 0.4 is 0.400, then 0.405, then 0.450. More digits do not make a number bigger.

items.title: Pounds against pence
items.prose: A share costs £2.40 and pays a dividend of 90p.
items.question: Write price : dividend in its simplest form.

options.why: You compared 2.40 with 90 without matching units. That sets pounds against pence.
You reversed the order. The price comes first.
You stopped early. 24 and 9 still share a factor of 3.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Write both in pence, then divide by the highest common factor.

explain.text: £2.40 is 240p, so the ratio is $240 : 90$. Both divide by 30, giving $8 : 3$.

items.title: How many tranches
items.prose: Work without a calculator. A fund splits £$4\tfrac{1}{2}$ million into tranches of £$\tfrac{3}{8}$ million each.
items.question: How many tranches does it fill?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count how many lots of $\tfrac{3}{8}$ fit into $4\tfrac{1}{2}$.

byKey.multiplied: You multiplied the two fractions. The question asks how many fit, which is a division.
byKey.flipped-first: You turned over the first fraction. Turn over the one you divide by.

explain.text: Dividing by $\tfrac{3}{8}$ is multiplying by $\tfrac{8}{3}$. So $\tfrac{9}{2} \times \tfrac{8}{3} = \tfrac{72}{6} = 12$. Check: $12 \times \tfrac{3}{8} = 4\tfrac{1}{2}$.

items.title: Which decimals stop
items.question: Which of these fractions are terminating decimals? Select all that apply.

options.why: You saw an even denominator. But 12 has a factor of 3, so $\tfrac{5}{12} = 0.41666\ldots$ recurs.
You saw the 10 in 30. Its factor of 3 stays after simplifying, so $\tfrac{11}{30} = 0.3666\ldots$ recurs.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Simplify each fraction, then look for prime factors other than 2 and 5 in the denominator.

explain.text: In lowest terms, a decimal stops when the denominator has only the prime factors 2 and 5. $\tfrac{9}{75} = \tfrac{3}{25}$ and $\tfrac{21}{56} = \tfrac{3}{8}$ pass once simplified. The denominators 12 and 30 keep a factor of 3.

items.title: Ticks in a big move
items.prose: Work without a calculator. A futures price moves in ticks worth $\text{£}8 \times 10^{-3}$ each. A position's value has moved by $\text{£}6 \times 10^{5}$.
items.question: How many ticks is that? Give the answer in standard form.

options.why: You divided correctly but stopped. Standard form needs a first number from 1 up to 10.
You moved the power the wrong way when you turned 0.75 into 7.5. The power must drop by one.
You added the powers. Dividing subtracts them: $5 - (-3) = 8$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Divide the numbers, subtract the powers, then tidy into standard form.

items.title: A negative fractional power
items.prose: Work without a calculator.
items.question: What is $\left(\dfrac{8}{27}\right)^{-\frac{2}{3}}$?

widget.accept: Any form equal to $\tfrac{9}{4}$, which is 2.25

feedback.correct: Turn over, cube root, then square.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Deal with the minus sign, then the cube root, then the square.

byKey.no-flip: You found $\left(\tfrac{8}{27}\right)^{\frac{2}{3}}$. The minus sign in the power turns the fraction over.
byKey.negative: You read the minus in the power as a minus sign on the answer. It means a reciprocal, not a negative.

explain.text: The minus sign turns the fraction over: $\left(\tfrac{27}{8}\right)^{\frac{2}{3}}$. The cube root of $\tfrac{27}{8}$ is $\tfrac{3}{2}$. Squaring gives $\tfrac{9}{4}$.

items.title: Which operation first
items.prose: Work without a calculator.
items.question: What is $20 - 4 \times (1 - 4)^2 \div 6$?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Brackets, then powers, then multiply and divide, then subtract.

byKey.left-to-right: You did $20 - 4$ first. Multiplying and dividing come before subtracting.
byKey.negative-square: You squared −3 to get −9. A negative times a negative is positive, so it is 9.

explain.text: The bracket is −3, and its square is 9. Then $4 \times 9 \div 6 = 6$. Last comes the subtraction: $20 - 6 = 14$.

items.title: An estimate first
items.prose: Estimate $\dfrac{612 \times 0.0487}{0.198}$ without a calculator.
items.question: Round each number to 1 significant figure. What is your estimate?

options.why: You divided by 2. The bottom rounds to 0.2, and dividing by 0.2 is multiplying by 5.
You multiplied by 0.2 instead of dividing by it.
You rounded 0.0487 to 0.5. Its first significant figure is in the hundredths, so it rounds to 0.05.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Round each number to its first significant figure, then work it out.

explain.text: The numbers round to 600, 0.05 and 0.2. Then $600 \times 0.05 = 30$ and $30 \div 0.2 = 150$. A calculator gives 150.5, so the estimate is close.

items.title: The price before the fall
items.prose: After a 15% fall, a share is priced at £306.
items.question: What was the price before the fall, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The new price is 85% of the old one. Divide by the multiplier.

byKey.added-back: You added 15% of £306. The 15% was taken from the old, larger price.
byKey.took-off: You took 15% off again. Undo the fall by dividing by 0.85.

explain.text: After a 15% fall the price is 85% of the old price, so $0.85p = 306$. Dividing gives $p = 360$. Check: 15% of £360 is £54, and $360 - 54 = 306$.

items.title: Three moves in a row
items.prose: A portfolio rises 25%, then falls 20%, then rises 10%.
items.question: What is the overall percentage change?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Turn each change into a multiplier and multiply them.

byKey.added: You added the percentages: $25 - 20 + 10$. Each change acts on a new value, so multiply.

explain.text: The multipliers are 1.25, 0.8 and 1.1. Their product is $1.25 \times 0.8 \times 1.1 = 1.1$, a rise of 10%. The first two cancel exactly, since $1.25 \times 0.8 = 1$.

items.title: From the gap to the whole
items.prose: Two partners split a profit in the ratio $5 : 3$. The first gets £840 more than the second.
items.question: What is the whole profit, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The gap between the shares is a number of parts. Find one part first.

byKey.gap-as-share: You treated £840 as the first partner's share. It is the difference between the two shares.
byKey.gap-as-total: You gave the gap. The question asks for the whole profit.

explain.text: The gap is $5 - 3 = 2$ parts, so one part is £420. The whole profit is $5 + 3 = 8$ parts: $8 \times 420 = 3360$. The shares are £2,100 and £1,260.

items.title: Through the pound
items.prose: The quoted rates: £1 buys 1.25 US dollars, and £1 buys 1.15 euros. A bond pays a 500 dollar coupon, and a broker charges a 1,840 euro fee.
items.question: Fill in the table.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. To turn a foreign amount into pounds, divide by its rate.

byKey.r0c1: Each pound is worth more than a dollar, so there are fewer pounds than dollars. Divide 500 by 1.25.
byKey.r0c2: Go through pounds: turn the dollars into pounds, then multiply by 1.15.
byKey.r1c1: Each pound buys 1.15 euros, so there are fewer pounds than euros. Divide 1,840 by 1.15.

explain.text: Each pound buys 1.25 dollars, so 500 dollars is $500 \div 1.25 = 400$ pounds. In euros that is $400 \times 1.15 = 460$. The fee is $1840 \div 1.15 = 1600$ pounds.

items.title: What share lost
items.prose: Of 1,250 trades last month, 85 lost money.
items.question: What percentage of the trades lost money?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Divide the part by the whole, then turn the decimal into a percentage.

byKey.flipped: You divided 1,250 by 85. Put the part over the whole.
byKey.decimal: You typed the decimal 0.068. As a percentage that is 6.8%.

explain.text: The part is 85 and the whole is 1,250. $\tfrac{85}{1250} = \tfrac{6.8}{100}$, which is 6.8%. Check: 10% of 1,250 is 125, and 85 is a bit over half of that.

items.title: A steady fill
items.prose: An algorithm buys 1,800 shares in 2.5 minutes, at a steady rate.
items.question: At the same rate, how many seconds does it take to buy 4,500 shares?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the shares bought per second, then divide 4,500 by it.

byKey.minutes: You found 6.25 minutes. The question asks for seconds.

explain.text: 2.5 minutes is 150 seconds, so the rate is $1800 \div 150 = 12$ shares a second. Then $4500 \div 12 = 375$ seconds. That is 6.25 minutes.

items.title: Three years of losses
items.prose: A trading server loses 20% of its value each year. After 3 years it is worth £10,240.
items.question: What was the server worth when new, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Each year multiplies the value by 0.8. Undo three of those.

byKey.simple: You took off 60% in one go. Each 20% is taken from a smaller value, so the losses are not 3 equal amounts.
byKey.added-back: You added 20% back each year. Each loss was 20% of a larger value, so divide by 0.8.

explain.text: Each year keeps 80% of the value, so after 3 years the value is $0.8^3 = 0.512$ of the price new. Then $10240 \div 0.512 = 20000$. Check: 20,000, 16,000, 12,800, 10,240.

items.title: Inverse to the square
items.prose: $y$ is inversely proportional to the square of $x$. When $x = 2$, $y = 12$.
items.question: Fill in the missing values of $y$. Give $y$ to 2 decimal places where needed.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find $k$ in $y = \tfrac{k}{x^2}$ from the given pair first.

byKey.r0c1: Halving $x$ multiplies $y$ by 4, because the rule uses the square of $x$. So $y = 48$, not 24.
byKey.r2c1: Doubling $x$ divides $y$ by 4 here, not by 2. Use $y = \tfrac{48}{x^2}$.

explain.text: From $12 = \tfrac{k}{2^2}$, $k = 48$, so $y = \tfrac{48}{x^2}$. Then $y$ is 48 at $x = 1$, 3 at $x = 4$ and $\tfrac{4}{3} \approx 1.33$ at $x = 6$. Doubling $x$ divides $y$ by 4.

items.title: Signs and powers
items.question: Which of these are equal to −8? Select all that apply.

options.why: A negative power turns the number over: $2^{-3} = \tfrac{1}{8}$. It is positive.
You stopped at $(-2)^3 = -8$. The minus in front turns it into 8.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work out the power first, then any minus sign written in front of it.

items.title: Two ratios joined
items.prose: Desks A, B and C share a £1,400 bonus. $A : B = 2 : 3$ and $B : C = 4 : 5$.
items.question: How much does C get, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Make B the same number of parts in both ratios first.

byKey.joined: You wrote $2 : 3 : 5$ and added the parts. B is 3 parts in one ratio and 4 in the other, so match B first.
byKey.two-only: You shared the £1,400 between B and C alone. A takes a share too.

explain.text: B is 3 parts in one ratio and 4 in the other, so scale both to 12: $A : B : C = 8 : 12 : 15$. That is 35 parts, so one part is $1400 \div 35 = 40$. C gets $15 \times 40 = 600$.

items.title: Fees on the way in and out
items.prose: You put £10,000 into a fund. It takes a 1.5% entry fee first, and the rest grows by 12%. Then the fund keeps 20% of any value above the £10,000 you paid in.
items.question: How much do you end with, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Take each step in order: the entry fee, the growth, then 20% of the value above £10,000.

byKey.skipped-entry: You grew the whole £10,000. The entry fee comes off before anything is invested.
byKey.fee-on-growth: You charged 20% on all the growth. The fee is only on the value above the £10,000 you paid in.
byKey.fee-on-all: You took 20% of the whole value. The fee is 20% of the part above £10,000.

explain.text: After the 1.5% fee, £9,850 is invested, and 12% growth makes $9850 \times 1.12 = 11032$. The value above £10,000 is £1,032, and 20% of it is £206.40. You keep $11032 - 206.40 = 10825.60$.

items.title: A recurring decimal as a fraction
items.prose: Show that $0.2\dot{3}\dot{6} = 0.2363636\ldots$ is equal to $\dfrac{13}{55}$. Only the 36 repeats.
items.question: Put the lines in order.

lines.text: Subtract: the repeating tails cancel, so $990x = 234$.

feedback.correct: Name it, line up two copies, subtract, simplify.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Each line needs the ones before it.

byKey.sub: You subtracted before both copies were written down. Write $1000x$ and $10x$ first.
byKey.end: The fraction comes last, once the subtraction has given $990x = 234$.

explain.text: Both $1000x$ and $10x$ end in the same repeating 36. Subtracting them leaves the whole number $990x = 234$. Dividing by 990 and cancelling 18 gives $\tfrac{13}{55}$.
